theorem TauCeti.ad_pow_lie_serreE_serreE : ∀ {B : Type u_1} [inst : DecidableEq B] (R : Type u_2) [inst_1 : CommRing R] (CM : Matrix B B ℤ) (i j : B),

      ⁅TauCeti.serreE R CM i, TauCeti.serreE R CM j⁆ =

docstring: The higher Serre relation on the `E`'s: `(ad Eᵢ) ^ (-CMᵢⱼ).toNat ⁅Eᵢ, Eⱼ⁆ = 0`.
description:
**Higher Serre relation for the generators $E_i$.** Let $B$ be a finite-or-arbitrary index set with decidable equality, let $R$ be a commutative ring, and let $CM = (CM_{ij})$ be an integer matrix (a generalized Cartan matrix in the Kac–Moody setting). Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be the Lie algebra over $R$ associated to $CM$, with Chevalley-type generators $E_i$ for $i \in B$. Then for all indices $i, j \in B$, applying the adjoint representation of $E_i$ to the power $(-CM_{ij})^+ = \max(-CM_{ij}, 0)$ times, and then evaluating on the Lie bracket $[E_i, E_j]$, gives zero:
$$\operatorname{ad}(E_i)^{\,-CM_{ij}}\big([E_i, E_j]\big) = 0,$$
where the exponent is taken to be the nonnegative integer $-CM_{ij}$ (and is zero when $CM_{ij} \ge 0$). In other words, $\operatorname{ad}(E_i)^{1-a_{ij}}(E_j) = 0$ type relations hold in the form stated, with the exponent being the truncation of $-CM_{ij}$ to a natural number.

at most `ε`.

`range (1 - P)` whose opening tends to `0` with the Lipschitz constant of the nonlinearity. This

**Norm bound for the local unstable graph map.** Let $A$ and $P$ be continuous linear maps on a complete real normed space $X$, and let $N : X \to X$ be $\varepsilon$-Lipschitz on the closed ball of radius $r \ge 0$ about $0$. Suppose the following hold:

- For all $t \le 0$ and $v \in X$, $\|e^{tA}(v - Pv)\| \le K e^{\alpha t}\|v\|$ (the unstable part decays backward in time).

The bigraded `Ext` groups of `(X, Y)` **assemble into the ungraded `Ext` groups** of a pair
`(X', Y')`: in every cohomological degree the direct sum over the internal degrees of
`Ext^n(X, Y{j})` is `Ext^n(X', Y')`.

This is the hypothesis under which a q-Euler form specializes at `q = 1` to an ordinary Ext-Euler

$$\text{Ext}^n_D(X', Y') \cong \bigoplus_{j \in \mathbb{Z}} \text{Ext}^n_C(X, Y\{j\}).$$

the positive nilpotent subalgebra `𝔫⁺` — the nilpotent ideal of the standard Borel subalgebra
`TauCeti.upperTriangular R n`, not an ideal of `gl n R` — so this says exactly that `v` is a

theorem SSet.mayerVietorisToBiprod_fromBiprod_assoc : ∀ {C : Type u} [inst : CategoryTheory.Category.{v, u} C] [inst_1 : CategoryTheory.Limits.HasCoproducts C]
  [inst_2 : CategoryTheory.Abelian C] (R : C) {X₁ X₂ X₃ X₄ : SSet} {t : X₁ ⟶ X₂} {l : X₁ ⟶ X₃} {r : X₂ ⟶ X₄}
  {b : X₃ ⟶ X₄},
  CategoryTheory.CommSq t l r b →
    ∀ (n : ℕ) {Z : C} (h : X₄.homology R n ⟶ Z),
      CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp (SSet.mayerVietorisToBiprod R t l n)
          (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp (SSet.mayerVietorisFromBiprod R r b n) h) =
        CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp 0 h
description:
**Vanishing of consecutive Mayer–Vietoris maps.** Let $R$ be an object of an abelian category with coproducts, and let
$$\begin{array}{ccc} X_1 & \xrightarrow{\ t\ } & X_2 \\ {\scriptstyle l}\downarrow & & \downarrow{\scriptstyle r} \\ X_3 & \xrightarrow{\ b\ } & X_4 \end{array}$$
be a commutative square of simplicial sets. For every natural number $n$ and every morphism $h\colon H_n(X_4;R)\to Z$, composing the Mayer–Vietoris map $H_n(X_1;R)\to H_n(X_2;R)\oplus H_n(X_3;R)$ with the Mayer–Vietoris map $H_n(X_2;R)\oplus H_n(X_3;R)\to H_n(X_4;R)$ and then with $h$ gives the zero morphism. In other words, two consecutive maps in the Mayer–Vietoris sequence compose to zero, so any further map applied to $H_n(X_4;R)$ kills their composite.

name: TauCeti.Multiquadratic.IsNarrowGenusField

docstring:
An abelian extension `L / ℚ`, with a chosen quadratic subfield generated by `y² = d`, is a
**narrow genus field** when it is unramified over that subfield at every finite place and is
maximal among abelian extensions with those properties.

field and the everywhere-unramified genus field for a real quadratic radicand.

name: TauCeti.IsChevalleySystem
signature:
structure TauCeti.IsChevalleySystem : {K : Type u} →
  {L : Type v} →
    [inst : Field K] →
      [inst_1 : LieRing L] →
        [inst_2 : LieAlgebra K L] →
          [LieAlgebra.IsKilling K L] →
            [FiniteDimensional K L] →
              {H : LieSubalgebra K L} →
                [inst_5 : H.IsCartanSubalgebra] →
                  [LieModule.IsTriangularizable K (↥H) L] → (L ≃ₗ⁅K⁆ L) → (LieModule.Weight K (↥H) L → L) → Prop
docstring:
A normalized family of root vectors compatible with a Chevalley involution. The Lie
automorphism `ω` exchanges each root vector with the negative of its opposite.

There is no separate involutivity field: `TauCeti.IsChevalleySystem.involutive` proves it from this
compatibility and the fact that the root vectors and Cartan subalgebra span the ambient Lie
algebra.
description: **Chevalley system relative to a Chevalley involution.** Let $L$ be a finite-dimensional Killing Lie algebra over a field $K$, with a Cartan subalgebra $H$ whose action on $L$ is triangularizable. Given a Lie algebra automorphism $\omega$ of $L$ and an assignment sending each root $\alpha$ (a weight of $H$ acting on $L$) to a vector $e_\alpha \in L$, the statement says that this family is a normalized family of root vectors compatible with $\omega$. Each $e_\alpha$ is a root vector, and $\omega$ exchanges $e_\alpha$ with the negative of the root vector for the opposite root, so that $\omega(e_\alpha) = -e_{-\alpha}$, with the normalization conditions also holding. No involutivity of $\omega$ is assumed separately, since it follows from this compatibility together with the fact that the root vectors and $H$ span $L$.

description: **Cyclicity of the Preimage of the $n$-Torsion Subgroup of an Additive Circle.** Let $p$ be a positive element of a strictly ordered field and let $\mathbb{T}_p$ denote the additive circle of period $p$. signature:
theorem ContinuousLinearMap.norm_localUnstableGraphMap_le : ∀ {X : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup X] [inst_1 : NormedSpace ℝ X] [inst_2 : CompleteSpace X] {K α ε : NNReal}
  {A P : X →L[ℝ] X} {N : X → X} {r : ℝ}
  (hs : ∀ (t : ℝ), 0 ≤ t → ∀ (v : X), ‖(NormedSpace.exp (t • A)) (P v)‖ ≤ ↑K * Real.exp (-↑α * t) * ‖v‖)

  (hN : LipschitzOnWith ε N (Metric.closedBall 0 r)) (hsmall : 2 * K * (ε * 2) < α),
  N 0 = 0 →
    ∀ (v : X),
      ‖A.localUnstableGraphMap P N r hs hu hr hN hsmall v‖ ≤
        ↑(2 * K * (ε * 2) / α * (K / (1 - 2 * K * (ε * 2) / α))) * ‖v‖

`range (1 - P)` whose opening tends to `0` with the Lipschitz constant of the nonlinearity. This
is the unstable counterpart of `ContinuousLinearMap.norm_localStableGraphMap_le`.
description: **Bound on the Lipschitz constant of the local unstable manifold map.** Consider a complete normed space $X$ and a continuous linear operator $A$ on $X$. Let $P$ be a projection such that the semigroup generated by $A$ is exponentially contracting on the range of $P$ for $t \ge 0$ (with constants $K$ and $\alpha$) and exponentially contracting on the range of $I - P$ for $t \le 0$. field and the everywhere-unramified genus field for a real quadratic radicand.
description: **Narrow Genus Field.** Let $d$ be an integer, let $L$ be a number field, and let $y \in L$ satisfy $y^2 = d$, so that $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{d})$ sits inside $L$ as a quadratic subfield. The predicate asserts that $L$ is a narrow genus field of $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{d})$ in the following sense: $L/\mathbb{Q}$ is an abelian extension, $L/\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{d})$ is unramified at every finite prime (no condition is imposed at the infinite places, so ramification at real places is allowed), and $L$ is maximal with respect to these two properties among abelian extensions of $\mathbb{Q}$. signature:
theorem TauCeti.enorm_setAverage_rpow_le : ∀ {α : Type u_1} {F : Type u_2} [inst : MeasurableSpace α] {mu : MeasureTheory.Measure α}
  [inst_1 : NormedAddCommGroup F] [inst_2 : NormedSpace ℝ F] {f : α → F} {s : Set α} {q : ℝ},
  1 ≤ q →
    MeasureTheory.AEStronglyMeasurable f mu →
      mu s ≠ 0 → mu s ≠ ⊤ → ‖⨍ (y : α) in s, f y ∂mu‖ₑ ^ q ≤ (mu s)⁻¹ * ∫⁻ (y : α) in s, ‖f y‖ₑ ^ q ∂mu
docstring:
**Hölder's bound on an average**, in `∫⁻` form: the `q`-th power of the average of `f` over a
set `s` of finite positive measure is at most `(μ s)⁻¹` times the integral of `‖f‖ ^ q` over `s`.
The single factor `(μ s)⁻¹` is what survives after the `q`-th power of the normalization
`(μ s)⁻¹` cancels against the `(μ s) ^ (q - 1)` of Hölder's inequality.
description:
**Hölder-type bound on the average of a function over a set.** Let $(\alpha, \mu)$ be a measure space, let $F$ be a normed real vector space, and let $f : \alpha \to F$ be almost everywhere strongly measurable with respect to $\mu$. Let $s \subseteq \alpha$ be a measurable set with $0 < \mu(s) < \infty$, and let $q \ge 1$ be a real number. Then the $q$-th power of the (extended) norm of the average of $f$ over $s$ is bounded by the average of the $q$-th power of the norm:

$$\Big\|\frac{1}{\mu(s)}\int_s f\,d\mu\Big\|^{q} \;\le\; \frac{1}{\mu(s)}\int_s \|f(y)\|^{q}\,d\mu(y),$$

where the integral on the right is a lower (extended nonnegative) Lebesgue integral, so the inequality holds in $[0,\infty]$ without any integrability assumption on $f$.

docstring:
A set `s` is **uniformly locally connected** if for every `ε > 0` there is a `δ > 0` such that
any two points of `s` at distance less than `δ` are joined by a connected subset of `s` of diameter
at most `ε`.

The smallness of the joining set is spelled out as a pairwise distance bound rather than as
`Metric.diam C ≤ ε`, because `Metric.diam` is `0` on an unbounded set, which would let an unbounded
`C` satisfy the condition vacuously. The lemma
`TauCeti.IsUniformlyLocallyConnected.exists_isConnected_diam_le` recovers the diameter phrasing,
boundedness of the joining set being one of its consequences.
description: **Uniformly locally connected set.** Let $X$ be a pseudo-metric space and let $S\subseteq X$. The set $S$ is uniformly locally connected if for every $\varepsilon>0$ there exists $\delta>0$ such that any two points $x,y\in S$ with distance $d(x,y)<\delta$ lie together in a connected subset $C\subseteq S$ whose pairwise distances are all at most $\varepsilon$; that is, $d(p,q)\le \varepsilon$ for all $p,q\in C$.

description: **Sign representation for the partition $(1^n)$.** For every natural number $n$, every permutation $\sigma$ of an $n$-element set, and every vector $x$ in the underlying space of the Specht module attached to the partition $(1^n)$ of $n$ (the partition into $n$ parts each equal to $1$), the action of $\sigma$ on $x$ is multiplication by the sign of $\sigma$, i.e. $\rho(\sigma)x = \operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\, x$, where $\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma) \in \{1,-1\}$ is viewed as a scalar in the base field. In other words, the Specht module $S^{(1^n)}$ is the sign representation of the symmetric group.

name: TauCeti.UniversalEnvelopingAlgebra.map_kostantToralWeylPoint
signature:
theorem TauCeti.UniversalEnvelopingAlgebra.map_kostantToralWeylPoint : ∀ {L : Type u} [inst : LieRing L] [inst_1 : LieAlgebra ℚ L] {I : Type w} {κ : Type} [inst_2 : Fintype κ] {V : Type}
  [inst_3 : AddCommGroup V] [inst_4 : Module ℚ V] (e : I → L) (h : κ → L)
  (ρ : UniversalEnvelopingAlgebra ℚ L →ₐ[ℚ] Module.End ℚ V) (M : AddSubgroup V)
  (hM : ∀ u ∈ TauCeti.UniversalEnvelopingAlgebra.kostantForm e h, ∀ m ∈ M, (ρ u) m ∈ M)
  (hnil : ∀ (i : I), IsNilpotent (ρ ((UniversalEnvelopingAlgebra.ι ℚ) (e i)))) {n : ℕ} (b : Module.Basis (Fin n) ℤ ↥M)
  (wt : Fin n → κ → ℤ) {A : Type v} {B : Type v'} [inst_5 : CommRing A] [inst_6 : CommRing B] (φ : A →+* B) (i j : I),
  (TauCeti.GeneralLinear.mapHopfIdealPointsSubgroup n
        (TauCeti.UniversalEnvelopingAlgebra.kostantToralDefiningIdeal e h ρ M hM hnil b wt) φ.toIntAlgHom)
      ((MulEquiv.subgroupCongr ⋯)
        (TauCeti.UniversalEnvelopingAlgebra.kostantToralWeylPoint e h ρ M hM hnil b wt i j A)) =
    (MulEquiv.subgroupCongr ⋯) (TauCeti.UniversalEnvelopingAlgebra.kostantToralWeylPoint e h ρ M hM hnil b wt i j B)
docstring:
The carrier's Weyl representative is natural in the value ring. Applying a ring homomorphism
entrywise sends the representative over the source ring to the representative over the target
ring.
description: **Naturality of the Kostant–Toral Weyl Point.** Let $L$ be a Lie algebra over $\mathbb{Q}$, let $e_i$ ($i\in I$) and $h_k$ ($k\in\kappa$, a finite index set) be given elements of $L$, and let $\rho$ be a representation of the universal enveloping algebra of $L$ on a $\mathbb{Q}$-vector space $V$ preserving a lattice $M$, in which each $\rho(e_i)$ is nilpotent. Fix a $\mathbb{Z}$-basis of $M$ and integer weight data $\mathrm{wt}$. For any commutative rings $A$ and $B$ and any ring homomorphism $\varphi: A \to B$, and for any indices $i,j\in I$, the Weyl group representative attached to the pair $(i,j)$ over $A$ (the point of the general linear group $\mathrm{GL}_n$ over $A$, viewed as a point of the subgroup cut out by the Kostant–Toral defining ideal, and transported along the canonical identification of that subgroup) is carried by $\varphi$ entrywise to the corresponding Weyl group representative over $B$. In other words, applying $\varphi$ to each matrix entry of the $A$-point gives exactly the $B$-point, so the assignment $A \mapsto$ (Weyl representative) is natural in the coefficient ring.

The inverse comparison sends an integral vector of the abstract complexification to the
corresponding nested pure tensor.
description: **Inverse Comparison of Integral Vectors.** For a $\mathbb{Z}$-linear map $\iota_{\mathbb{C}} : V \to V_{\mathbb{C}}$ that exhibits $V_{\mathbb{C}}$ as the complexification of an abelian group $V$ (via base change to $\mathbb{C}$), the inverse of the natural equivalence between the realification of $V_{\mathbb{C}}$ and $\mathbb{R} \otimes_{\mathbb{Z}} V$ maps the image of any $x \in V$ under $\iota_{\mathbb{C}}$ to the pure tensor $1 \otimes_{\mathbb{R}} (1 \otimes_{\mathbb{Z}} x)$.

name: TauCeti.IsHyperellipticFunctionField
signature: structure TauCeti.IsHyperellipticFunctionField : (k : Type u_3) → (F : Type u_4) → [inst : Field k] → [inst_1 : Field F] → [Algebra k F] → Prop
docstring:
A **hyperelliptic function field** (Stichtenoth, Definition 6.2.1, with separability of the
index-two subextension made part of the definition): genus at least two together with an element
`x` transcendental over `k` such that `F / k(x)` is separable of degree two.

Being an algebraic function field is *not* part of the predicate: the hypothesis
`TauCeti.IsFunctionField`, like the exactness of the constant field, is kept as a separate
hypothesis on the statements that need it, as everywhere in this development.

In characteristic two an index-two subextension can be purely inseparable, and such an `F` is
deliberately outside this model class; away from characteristic two the separability clause is
automatic, so there the predicate agrees with Stichtenoth's index-two definition.
description: **Hyperelliptic Function Field.** A field extension $F/k$ is a hyperelliptic function field if $F$ has genus at least two and there exists an element $x \in F$, transcendental over $k$, such that the extension $F/k(x)$ is a separable quadratic extension.

The ideal defining the kernel of `D(N) → D(M)` is the kernel of the coordinate

theorem AddCircle.exists_zsmul_eq_of_apply_eq_coe_period_div : ∀ {𝕜 : Type u_1} [inst : Field 𝕜] [inst_1 : LinearOrder 𝕜] [IsStrictOrderedRing 𝕜] (p : 𝕜) [hp : Fact (0 < p)] {n : ℕ}

docstring:
The element of invariant `p / n` generates a group carrying an invariant map onto the
`n`-torsion.
description: **Generator of a torsion-isomorphic group.** Let $\mathbb{K}$ be a linearly ordered field with $p > 0$, let $n$ be a positive natural number, and let $H$ be an additive group. Suppose $f : H \to \mathbb{R}/p\mathbb{Z}$ is an injective group homomorphism whose image is exactly the subgroup of $n$-torsion elements of the circle $\mathbb{R}/p\mathbb{Z}$. If $u \in H$ satisfies $f(u) = [p/n]$, the class of $p/n$ in the circle, then every element $x \in H$ is an integer multiple of $u$. In other words, $H$ is cyclic and generated by $u$.

docstring: Transposing the last two indices negates the relator.
description: **Antisymmetry of the atom relator in the last two indices.** Let $R$ be a commutative ring and let $W:\mathbb{Z}\to R$ be an odd function, meaning $W(-n)=-W(n)$ for all integers $n$. Then the atom relator determined by $W$ changes sign when its last two arguments are swapped: for all integers $a,b,c,d$, the value at $(a,b,c,d)$ is the negative of the value at $(a,b,d,c)$.

name: TauCeti.WassersteinSpace.pseudoEMetricSpace
signature:
def TauCeti.WassersteinSpace.pseudoEMetricSpace : {X : Type u} →
  {p : ENNReal} →
    [inst : MeasurableSpace X] →
      [inst_1 : PseudoMetricSpace X] →
        [StandardBorelSpace X] →
          (Measurable fun z => edist z.1 z.2) → 1 ≤ p → PseudoEMetricSpace (TauCeti.WassersteinSpace p X)
docstring:
The Wasserstein extended distance equips finite-moment laws with a pseudoemetric space
structure whenever the ground distance is measurable and `1 ≤ p`.
description: **Wasserstein Space Pseudo-Extended-Metric Structure.** Let $X$ be a standard Borel space equipped with a pseudometric $d$ such that the distance function $(x,y)\mapsto d(x,y)$ is measurable, and let $p \ge 1$ be an extended nonnegative real exponent. Then the space of probability laws on $X$ with finite $p$-th moment, equipped with the $p$-Wasserstein extended distance, carries the structure of a pseudo-extended-metric space. In other words, the Wasserstein extended distance is a well-defined extended pseudometric on this space of finite-moment laws (it is symmetric, satisfies the triangle inequality, and assigns zero distance to a law from itself, while allowing distinct laws to be at distance zero), and this structure is given by the hypotheses above.

name: Nat.ordCompl_minFac_lt
signature: theorem Nat.ordCompl_minFac_lt : ∀ {n : ℕ}, 1 < n → n / n.minFac ^ n.factorization n.minFac < n
docstring: Peeling the block at the least prime factor makes `n` strictly smaller.
description: **Strict decrease after removing the least prime's block.** For every natural number $n > 1$, let $p$ be the smallest prime dividing $n$, and let $p^k$ be the largest power of $p$ dividing $n$, so $k \ge 1$ is the exact exponent of $p$ in $n$. Then dividing $n$ by $p^k$ gives a quotient strictly smaller than $n$.

name: TauCeti.tendsto_truncatedPerronKernel
signature:
theorem TauCeti.tendsto_truncatedPerronKernel : ∀ {x c : ℝ},

docstring:
As the height tends to infinity the truncated Perron kernel tends to the sharp step, at every
positive `x`; at the endpoint `x = 1` this is the half-weight limit
`TauCeti.tendsto_truncatedPerronKernel_one`.
description: **Convergence of the truncated Perron kernel to the sharp Perron step.** For any positive real numbers \(x\) and \(c\), as the height parameter tends to infinity, the truncated Perron kernel evaluated at \(x\) with parameter \(c\) converges to the value of the sharp Perron step at \(x\).

name: TauCeti.FramedMarkovBraid
signature: structure TauCeti.FramedMarkovBraid : Type
docstring:
A framed oriented braid-closure presentation. The braid direction supplies the orientation.
A framing of an oriented link in `S³`, relative to the Seifert framing, is specified by one
integer coefficient on each component; the components of a braid closure are the orbits of its
underlying permutation. The projection `forgetFraming` drops this data to the ordinary unframed
braid on which `TauCeti.MarkovEquiv` is defined.
description: **Framed Oriented Braid-Closure.** A framed oriented braid-closure is a mathematical structure representing an oriented link in $S^3$ equipped with a framing. The orientation of the link is induced by the braid direction, and the framing is defined relative to the Seifert framing by assigning an integer coefficient to each connected component of the link. These components correspond to the orbits of the permutation underlying the braid. The structure includes a projection that recovers the underlying unframed braid by forgetting the integer framing coefficients.

name: TauCeti.realCliffordZeroOneIsometry_apply
signature: theorem TauCeti.realCliffordZeroOneIsometry_apply : ∀ (v : Fin (0 + 1) → ℝ), TauCeti.realCliffordZeroOneIsometry v = v 0
docstring: `realCliffordZeroOneIsometry` reads off the single coordinate.
description: **Real Clifford zero-one isometry evaluation.** The real Clifford zero-one isometry acts on a real-valued vector indexed by a one-element index set by returning its sole coordinate. Equivalently, for every function $v$ assigning a real number to the unique index, applying the isometry to $v$ yields $v(0)$, the value at that single coordinate.

name: TauCeti.GridDiagram.twoByTwo_X
signature: theorem TauCeti.GridDiagram.twoByTwo_X : TauCeti.GridDiagram.twoByTwo.X = TauCeti.GridState.twoByTwoSwap
docstring: The `X`-marking state of the standard two-by-two diagram is the transposition state.
description: **Marking of the standard two-by-two diagram.** The $X$-marking of the standard two-by-two grid diagram equals the transposition grid state (the state obtained by swapping the two entries).

name: TauCeti.kroneckerLineRepScalar_intertwine
signature:
theorem TauCeti.kroneckerLineRepScalar_intertwine : ∀ {k : Type u} [inst : Field k] {A : Type v} {a₁ : A} {c d : k} [Nontrivial A]
  (e : TauCeti.kroneckerLineRep k a₁ c ⟶ TauCeti.kroneckerLineRep k a₁ d),
  c * TauCeti.kroneckerLineRepScalar e = d * TauCeti.kroneckerLineRepScalar e
docstring:
**On a quiver carrying more than one arrow the scalars of the two lines agree on the scalar of
any morphism between them**, by naturality along the distinguished arrow. The hypothesis
`Nontrivial A` is the existence of an arrow other than the distinguished one: it forces the two
components of the morphism to agree.
description: **Scalar agreement for morphisms between Kronecker line representations.** Let $k$ be a field, $A$ a nontrivial type (so that there exists an arrow of the quiver other than a fixed distinguished one), and $a_1 \in A$ the distinguished arrow. For any scalars $c, d \in k$ and any morphism $e$ from the Kronecker line representation with parameter $c$ to the Kronecker line representation with parameter $d$ (both built on the distinguished arrow $a_1$), the scalar attached to $e$ satisfies $c\cdot \lambda(e) = d\cdot \lambda(e)$, where $\lambda(e)$ denotes the scalar of the morphism $e$. Equivalently, $(c-d)\,\lambda(e) = 0$.

name: Module.Basis.coord_map_apply
signature:
theorem Module.Basis.coord_map_apply : ∀ {R : Type u_4} {M : Type u_5} {M' : Type u_6} {ι : Type u_7} [inst : Semiring R] [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid M]
  [inst_2 : Module R M] [inst_3 : AddCommMonoid M'] [inst_4 : Module R M'] (b : Module.Basis ι R M) (f : M ≃ₗ[R] M')

docstring:
The coordinates with respect to the basis `b.map f` transported along a linear equivalence
`f` are the coordinates with respect to `b` of the vector transported back along `f`. Not a simp
lemma: simp already unfolds the left side through `Module.Basis.coord_apply`.
description: **Coordinate Map of a Transported Basis.** Given a basis $b = \{e_i\}_{i \in I}$ for a module $M$ over a semiring $R$ and a linear equivalence $f: M \cong M'$, the $i$-th coordinate of a vector $x \in M'$ with respect to the transported basis $f(b)$ is equal to the $i$-th coordinate of $f^{-1}(x)$ with respect to the original basis $b$.

name: TauCeti.stabilizer_rootSet_mk
signature:
theorem TauCeti.stabilizer_rootSet_mk : ∀ {F : Type u_1} [inst : Field F] {M : Type u_2} [inst_1 : Field M] [inst_2 : Algebra F M] {q : Polynomial F} {α : M}
  (hα : α ∈ q.rootSet M), MulAction.stabilizer Gal(M/F) ⟨α, hα⟩ = MulAction.stabilizer Gal(M/F) α
docstring:
The stabilizer of a root, as a point of the root set, is its stabilizer as an element of the
field.
description: **Stabilizer of a root as a point of the root set.** Let $F$ be a field, $M$ a field extension of $F$, and $q$ a polynomial over $F$. Let $\alpha \in M$ be a root of $q$ in $M$, so that $\alpha$ lies in the root set of $q$ in $M$. Then the stabilizer of $\alpha$, viewed as an element of the root set, under the action of the Galois group $\mathrm{Gal}(M/F)$ on the root set, coincides with the stabilizer of $\alpha$ viewed as an element of $M$ under the action of $\mathrm{Gal}(M/F)$ on $M$. In other words, the subgroup of automorphisms in $\mathrm{Gal}(M/F)$ fixing $\alpha$ is the same whether one regards $\alpha$ as a root point or as a field element.

name: HeckeRing.GLn.CanonicalDiagonal
signature: def HeckeRing.GLn.CanonicalDiagonal : ℕ → Type
docstring:
The positive divisibility chains of length `n`: the parameter space of the diagonal
double cosets.
description: **Canonical Diagonal Parameter Space.** For each natural number $n$, this is the collection of positive divisibility chains of length $n$, serving as the parameter space for the diagonal double cosets in the $\mathrm{GL}_n$ Hecke ring.

name: TauCeti.HeegaardIntersectionSystem
signature: structure TauCeti.HeegaardIntersectionSystem : ℕ → Type u → Type u
docstring:
Finite intersection data for two equally sized curve systems. The finite enumeration records
the point set, and each point has one `α`-curve label and one `β`-curve label; geometric surface
and region data are additional structure.
description: **Heegaard Intersection System.** For a natural number $g$ and a type $\alpha$ of points, a Heegaard intersection system of genus $g$ consists of finite intersection data for two families of $g$ curves, one family labelled by $\alpha$-curves and the other by $\beta$-curves. Concretely, it is a finite set of intersection points together with, for each point, a label identifying one $\alpha$-curve and one $\beta$-curve passing through it. The structure records only this combinatorial incidence data; any geometric information about the underlying surface or the regions it cuts out is extra structure carried alongside, not part of this basic data.

name: TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.Modulus.lcm_dvd

theorem TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.Modulus.lcm_dvd : ∀ {K : Type u_1} [inst : Field K] [inst_1 : NumberField K] {m n p : TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.Modulus K},

docstring: The least common multiple divides every common multiple.
description: **Divisibility of the Least Common Multiple.** For any moduli $m, n,$ and $p$ in a number field $K$, if $m$ divides $p$ and $n$ divides $p$, then the least common multiple of $m$ and $n$ also divides $p$.

name: TauCeti.PrimeBoundaryRemainder

structure TauCeti.PrimeBoundaryRemainder : (K : Type u_2) →

**Boundary data for the prime Dirichlet series of `S`.**  The function `series` is the sum
of the Dirichlet series of `primeVonMangoldtCoeff K S` on `Re s > 1`.  The function `remainder`
is continuous on `Re s ≥ 1` and agrees on the open half-plane with
`series s - δ / (s - 1)`.

The functions have precisely their mathematically relevant domains, so the structure carries no
arbitrary values elsewhere.

name: TauCeti.levelSetChartModel_source
signature:
theorem TauCeti.levelSetChartModel_source : ∀ {𝕜 : Type u_1} [inst : NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] {E : Type u_2} [inst_1 : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  [inst_2 : NormedSpace 𝕜 E] [inst_3 : CompleteSpace E] {F : Type u_3} [inst_4 : NormedAddCommGroup F]
  [inst_5 : NormedSpace 𝕜 F] [inst_6 : CompleteSpace F] {f : E → F} {f' : E →L[𝕜] F} {a : E} {c : F}
  [inst_7 : CompleteSpace 𝕜] {n : ℕ} (hf : HasStrictFDerivAt f f' a) (hf' : (↑f').range = ⊤)
  (hker : (↑f').ker.ClosedComplemented) (hfin : FiniteDimensional 𝕜 ↥(↑f').ker) (hn : Module.finrank 𝕜 ↥(↑f').ker = n)
  (ha : f a = c),
  (TauCeti.levelSetChartModel hf hf' hker hfin hn ha).source = (TauCeti.levelSetChart hf hf' hker ha).source
docstring: The model chart has the same source as the chart of the level set it is read from.
description: **Source of the Level-Set Model Chart.** Let $\mathbb{K}$ be a nontrivially normed, complete field, let $E$ and $F$ be complete normed spaces over $\mathbb{K}$, and let $f : E \to F$ be a function that is strictly differentiable at a point $a \in E$ with derivative $f' : E \to_L F$. Suppose that $f'$ is surjective, that its kernel is closed and complemented in $E$, and that the kernel is finite-dimensional of dimension $n$. Let $c = f(a)$. Then the source (domain) of the model chart for the level set $\{f = c\}$ constructed from these data coincides with the source of the level-set chart itself. In other words, the model chart and the level-set chart are defined on the same open set.

name: TauCeti.GLSymplecticFin.RootSubgroupIndex
signature: inductive TauCeti.GLSymplecticFin.RootSubgroupIndex : ℕ → Type
docstring:
An extensional index for the root one-parameter subgroups of the standard symplectic group.

Difference roots retain their ordered pair of indices. The symmetric positive- and negative-sum
roots store their indices in increasing order, so each root has only one index.
description: **Extensional Root Subgroup Index.** For each natural number $n$, this gives an extensional indexing scheme for the root one-parameter subgroups of the standard symplectic group. Difference roots retain their ordered pair of indices, while symmetric positive-sum and negative-sum roots are indexed by a single index obtained by arranging the relevant indices in increasing order.

name: TauCeti.ClassFunction.indVirtualCharacters
signature:
def TauCeti.ClassFunction.indVirtualCharacters : (k : Type u) →
  (G : Type v) → [inst : Field k] → [inst_1 : Group G] → [Finite G] → (Subgroup G → Prop) → AddSubgroup (G → k)
docstring:
**The virtual characters of `G` induced from a family of subgroups**: the additive subgroup of
`G → k` generated by `Ind_S^G ψ` for `S` satisfying `P` and `ψ` a virtual character of `S`.

For `P` the cyclic or elementary subgroups this is the subgroup generated by induction from their
virtual-character lattices; it is the image of the induction map `⨁_S R(S) → R(G)`.
description: **Subgroup of virtual characters induced from a family of subgroups.** Let $k$ be a field and $G$ a finite group, and let $P$ be a property of subgroups of $G$. This defines an additive subgroup of the group of $k$-valued class functions on $G$ (functions $G \to k$). It is the additive subgroup generated by all induced class functions $\operatorname{Ind}_S^G \psi$, where $S$ ranges over subgroups of $G$ satisfying $P$ and $\psi$ ranges over virtual characters of $S$. In particular, when $P$ picks out the cyclic subgroups (or the elementary subgroups), this is the subgroup obtained by inducing the virtual character lattices of those subgroups up to $G$; equivalently, it is the image of the induction map $\bigoplus_S R(S) \to R(G)$.

name: TauCeti.hermiteDilated
signature: def TauCeti.hermiteDilated : ℕ → Polynomial ℝ
docstring:
The dilated Hermite polynomial `Hₙ(√2 · X)`, the polynomial whose Gaussian envelope is the
Hermite function `ψₙ`.

It is defined at this layer rather than at the basis layer because every `MemLp` result below is
already about it: `ψₙ` *is* this polynomial times `exp(-x²/2)`, up to normalization.
description: **Dilated Hermite polynomial.** For each natural number $n$, this defines the real polynomial $H_n(\sqrt{2}\,X)$, obtained from the $n$-th Hermite polynomial $H_n$ by replacing its variable with $\sqrt{2}$ times the indeterminate $X$. The polynomial is the Gaussian-envelope factor of the $n$-th Hermite function $\psi_n$: multiplying it by $\exp(-x^2/2)$ gives $\psi_n$ up to a normalization constant.

name: TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.ideleCongruenceSubgroup
signature:
def TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.ideleCongruenceSubgroup : {K : Type u_1} →
  [inst : Field K] →
    [inst_1 : NumberField K] →
      TauCeti.GlobalNumberFields.Modulus K → Subgroup (NumberField.IdeleGroup (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K) K)
docstring:
**The idele congruence subgroup of a modulus**: the ideles congruent to one modulo `𝔪` that
are moreover units of the valuation ring at the finite places not dividing `𝔪`.  Explicitly, they
are principal units of the prescribed level at the finite divisors of `𝔪`, units of the valuation
ring at the remaining finite places, and positive at the real places selected by `𝔪`.  No
condition is imposed at the infinite places outside `𝔪`.

name: TauCeti.IsHyperellipticFunctionField

docstring:
A **hyperelliptic function field** (Stichtenoth, Definition 6.2.1, with separability of the
index-two subextension made part of the definition): genus at least two together with an element
`x` transcendental over `k` such that `F / k(x)` is separable of degree two.

Being an algebraic function field is *not* part of the predicate: the hypothesis
`TauCeti.IsFunctionField`, like the exactness of the constant field, is kept as a separate
hypothesis on the statements that need it, as everywhere in this development.

In characteristic two an index-two subextension can be purely inseparable, and such an `F` is
deliberately outside this model class; away from characteristic two the separability clause is
automatic, so there the predicate agrees with Stichtenoth's index-two definition.
description: **Hyperelliptic function field.** A field extension $F/k$ is hyperelliptic when its genus is at least two and there exists an element $x\in F$ transcendental over $k$ such that $F$ is a separable extension of $k(x)$ of degree two. This condition does not itself assert that $F$ is an algebraic function field over $k$; that is assumed separately when needed. In characteristic two, purely inseparable quadratic subextensions are excluded by the separability requirement, while away from characteristic two separability is automatic and the definition agrees with the usual index-two notion.

Weierstrass polynomial. It indexes the variables of `MvPolynomial Coeff ℤ = ℤ[A₁,⋯,A₆]`, the ring
the universal curve is defined over. There is no `A₅` — the subscripts are weights, not positions —
and the constructors are uppercase as names of indeterminates: `specialize` sends `A₁` to `W.a₁`.
description: **Weierstrass coefficient index set.** This is a five-element type whose elements label the coefficients $a_1, a_2, a_3, a_4, a_6$ of a Weierstrass equation, with the elements corresponding to the indeterminates $A_1, A_2, A_3, A_4, A_6$ of the polynomial ring $\mathbb{Z}[A_1, A_2, A_3, A_4, A_6]$ over which the universal Weierstrass curve is defined. Note that there is no index corresponding to $a_5$: the subscripts are weights (as in the weighted grading of Weierstrass coefficients) rather than positions in a list. Specializing an indeterminate $A_i$ to a given Weierstrass curve $W$ yields the corresponding coefficient $a_i$ of $W$.

**narrow genus field** when it is unramified over that subfield at every finite place and is

description: **Narrow Genus Field.** Let $L$ be an abelian extension of $\mathbb{Q}$ and let $d \in \mathbb{Z}$ be a square-free integer such that $L$ contains the quadratic subfield $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{d})$. description: **Inverse of a Trivial-Group Point.** For any commutative semirings $R$ and $A$ where $A$ is an $R$-algebra, the evaluation of the inverse of an element $f$ in the trivial group of $R$-algebra homomorphisms from $R$ to $A$ at a point $r \in R$ is equal to the image of $r$ under the canonical algebra map from $R$ to $A$.

For an arbitrary normal subgroup `H`, the action of `G ⧸ H` on the invariants `M ^ H` of a
discrete module is continuous. Unlike
`TauCeti.continuousSMulQuotientFixedPoints`, which reads the continuity off the discreteness of
`G ⧸ H` for open `H` and needs no continuity of the `G`-action, this deduces it from continuity of
the `G`-action: the invariants are discrete, so continuity is continuity in the group variable
alone, and there it is the continuity of the `G`-action read through the quotient map. No
compatibility of the topology of `G` with its group structure is needed, since `G ⧸ H` carries the
quotient topology.

For an element $x \in F$, if the universal Kähler differential $D_{F/k}(x)$ is nonzero, then $x$ is transcendental over $k$. name: TauCeti.realCliffordBottEquiv_ι
signature:
theorem TauCeti.realCliffordBottEquiv_ι : ∀ (p q : ℕ) (v : Fin (p + 1 + (q + 1)) → ℝ),
  (TauCeti.realCliffordBottEquiv p q) ((CliffordAlgebra.ι (TauCeti.realCliffordForm (p + 1) (q + 1))) v) =
    (CliffordAlgebra.ι (TauCeti.realCliffordForm p q)) ((TauCeti.realBottSplitIsometry p q) v).1 ⊗ₜ[ℝ] !![0, 1; 1, 0] +
      1 ⊗ₜ[ℝ]
        !![((TauCeti.realBottSplitIsometry p q) v).2 0, ((TauCeti.realBottSplitIsometry p q) v).2 1;
          -((TauCeti.realBottSplitIsometry p q) v).2 1, -((TauCeti.realBottSplitIsometry p q) v).2 0]
docstring:
`realCliffordBottEquiv` first separates the last positive and negative coordinates, then
applies the hyperbolic-plane equivalence.
description:
**Bott Equivalence on Generators.** For natural numbers $p, q$ and any vector $v$ in $\mathbb{R}^{(p+1)+(q+1)}$, equipped with the quadratic form of signature $(p+1, q+1)$, the Bott equivalence $\mathrm{Cl}(\mathbb{R}^{p+1,q+1}) \to \mathrm{Cl}(\mathbb{R}^{p,q}) \otimes \mathrm{Cl}(\mathbb{R}^{1,1})$ sends the image of $v$ under the canonical generator map to the following element. Let $(w, (a, b))$ be the components of the split isometry applied to $v$, where $w$ is a vector in the $(p,q)$-part and $(a,b)$ is a pair of reals. Then the image equals

$$\iota(w) \otimes \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix} \;+\; 1 \otimes \begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ -b & -a \end{pmatrix},$$

where $\iota(w)$ is the canonical generator image of $w$ in $\mathrm{Cl}(\mathbb{R}^{p,q})$. In words, the equivalence first splits off the last positive and negative coordinates of $v$ (via the split isometry), and then applies the hyperbolic-plane equivalence, so that the generator $v$ is mapped to the stated sum of tensors.

signature:
theorem TauCeti.NumberFieldArithmetic.artinElementAway_eq_of_isArithFrobAt : ∀ {K : Type u_1} [inst : Field K] [inst_1 : NumberField K] {L : Type u_2} [inst_2 : Field L] [inst_3 : NumberField L]
  [inst_4 : Algebra K L] [inst_5 : IsGalois K L] (hab : ∀ (σ τ : Gal(L/K)), Commute σ τ)
  (S : Finset (IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K)))
  (hur :
    ∀ v ∉ S,
      ∀ (Q : Ideal (NumberField.RingOfIntegers L)) [inst_6 : Q.IsPrime] [Q.LiesOver v.asIdeal],
        Algebra.IsUnramifiedAt (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K) Q)
  {v : IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K)},
  v ∉ S →
    ∀ (Q : Ideal (NumberField.RingOfIntegers L)) [Q.IsPrime] [Q.LiesOver v.asIdeal] {σ : Gal(L/K)},
      IsArithFrobAt (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K) σ Q → TauCeti.NumberFieldArithmetic.artinElementAway hab S hur v = σ
docstring:
**The Artin automorphism at `v ∉ S` is the Frobenius there.** Any arithmetic Frobenius at any
prime above `v` equals it, which is what makes the assignment `v ↦ artinElementAway hab S hur v`
well defined without a choice of prime above `v`.
description: **Artin automorphism at unramified places is the Frobenius.** Let $K \subseteq L$ be a Galois extension of number fields whose Galois group is abelian, and let $S$ be a finite set of nonzero primes of $\mathcal{O}_K$ such that every prime $v \notin S$ is unramified in $L$ (in the sense that every prime $Q$ of $\mathcal{O}_L$ lying over $v$ is unramified over $\mathcal{O}_K$). Let $v$ be a prime of $\mathcal{O}_K$ not in $S$, and let $Q$ be any prime of $\mathcal{O}_L$ lying over $v$. If $\sigma \in \mathrm{Gal}(L/K)$ is an arithmetic Frobenius element at $Q$, then the Artin automorphism assigned to $v$ (the element $\mathrm{artinElementAway}$ attached to $v$) is equal to $\sigma$. In other words, every arithmetic Frobenius at any prime above $v$ coincides with the Artin symbol of $v$, so the assignment $v \mapsto \sigma_v$ is independent of the choice of prime above $v$.

contains every canonical component of each of its elements, then it is the internal sum of its

If a submodule $p \subseteq V$ is stable under the projection onto each component $A_i$—that is, for every $m \in p$, each component of $m$ in the direct sum decomposition also belongs to $p$—then $p$ is equal to the supremum (or sum) of its intersections with each summand $A_i$.

Then the induced quotient map from $A$ by $K$ (defined using the inclusion $K \le \operatorname{rad}(A)$) sends $x$ to its equivalence class $x + (\text{radical part})$ in the quotient, i.e. the class of $x$ under the canonical quotient projection.

signature:
theorem TauCeti.ExactStructure.suspensionToStableOfPresentationsIso_inv_app : ∀ {C : Type u} [inst : CategoryTheory.Category.{v, u} C] [inst_1 : CategoryTheory.Preadditive C]
  [inst_2 : CategoryTheory.Limits.HasZeroObject C] [inst_3 : CategoryTheory.Limits.HasBinaryBiproducts C]
  {E : TauCeti.ExactStructure C} (P Q : (X : C) → E.InjectivePresentation X) (hP : ∀ (X : C), E.isProjective (P X).I)
  (hQ : ∀ (X : C), E.isProjective (Q X).I) (X : C),
  (E.suspensionToStableOfPresentationsIso P Q hP hQ).inv.app X =
    CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp (CategoryTheory.eqToHom ⋯)
      (CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp ((P X).projectiveStableIso (Q X) ⋯ ⋯).inv (CategoryTheory.eqToHom ⋯))
docstring:
The inverse of the comparison of two choices of relative injective presentations is the
comparison taken in the other order.
description: **Inverse of the suspension-to-stable comparison isomorphism.** Let $C$ be a preadditive category with a zero object and binary biproducts, and let $E$ be an exact structure on $C$. Given two families $P$ and $Q$ of injective presentations (one for each object $X$), whose injective objects are projective in $E$, the comparison natural isomorphism between the suspension-to-stable functors built from $P$ and from $Q$ has inverse at each object $X$ equal to the composite of an identity-type morphism (an `eqToHom`, which only rewrites between equal objects), the inverse of the canonical isomorphism between the projective stable objects $P_X$ and $Q_X$ at $X$, and another `eqToHom`. In other words, the inverse of the comparison at $X$ is the comparison taken in the opposite direction, so it is the inverse of the stable isomorphism comparing the two presentations of $X$, up to these trivial identifications.

Two fibre points have the same deck-orbit class exactly when they lie in the same deck
orbit. This uses the orientation of `MulAction.orbitRel_apply`: the left point is a member of
the orbit of the right point.
description: **Fibre orbit classes.** Let $p : E \to B$ be a map from a topological space $E$ to a set $B$, and fix a point $b \in B$. For two points $e, e'$ in the fibre $p^{-1}(\{b\})$, the deck-orbit classes of $e$ and $e'$ coincide if and only if $e$ lies in the orbit of $e'$ under the action of the deck group of $p$; that is, $e = g\cdot e'$ for some deck transformation $g$ of $p$.

docstring: Bundled unit-disc form of the Schwarz--Pick contraction estimate.
description:
**Schwarz–Pick contraction for the unit disc.** Let $f:\mathbb{C}\to\mathbb{C}$ be a function that is complex differentiable on the open unit disc $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}: |z|<1\}$ and maps $\mathbb{D}$ into itself. Then for all $z,w\in\mathbb{D}$, the pseudo-hyperbolic distance between $f(z)$ and $f(w)$ is at most the pseudo-hyperbolic distance between $z$ and $w$, namely
$$\left|\frac{f(z)-f(w)}{1-\overline{f(w)}\,f(z)}\right| \le \left|\frac{z-w}{1-\overline{w}\,z}\right|,$$
where the pseudo-hyperbolic expression is understood in the standard sense for points of the unit disc.

description: **Multiplicativity of an ideal arithmetic function.** Let $K$ be a field (in the setting of ideals of a Dedekind-type ring of integers of $K$), and let $f$ be an ideal arithmetic function, i.e. a function assigning a value to each nonzero ideal. docstring:
**The idele congruence subgroup of a modulus**: the ideles congruent to one modulo `𝔪` that
are moreover units of the valuation ring at the finite places not dividing `𝔪`.  Explicitly, they
are principal units of the prescribed level at the finite divisors of `𝔪`, units of the valuation
ring at the remaining finite places, and positive at the real places selected by `𝔪`.  No
condition is imposed at the infinite places outside `𝔪`.
description:
**Idele congruence subgroup.** Let $K$ be a number field and let $\mathfrak{m}$ be a modulus of $K$ (a formal product of finite primes of $K$, together with a choice of real places). The idele congruence subgroup attached to $\mathfrak{m}$ is the subgroup of the idele group of $K$ consisting of those ideles $x = (x_v)_v$ satisfying the following local conditions:

- At each finite place $v$ dividing $\mathfrak{m}$, the component $x_v$ is a principal unit of the prescribed level, i.e. $x_v \equiv 1$ modulo the corresponding power of $v$.
- At each finite place $v$ not dividing $\mathfrak{m}$, the component $x_v$ is a unit of the valuation ring $\mathcal{O}_v$ (so $x_v \in \mathcal{O}_v^\times$).
- At each real place selected by $\mathfrak{m}$, the component $x_v$ is positive.
- At the infinite places not selected by $\mathfrak{m}$, no condition is imposed.

The statement defines this set as a subgroup of the idele group of $K$, which is the standard congruence subgroup of ideles determined by the modulus $\mathfrak{m}$.

internal-hom degree `p + q`.
description: **Dual-tensor maps lie in the internal-hom piece of degree $p+q$.** Let $W_1$ and $W_2$ be complex vector spaces, each equipped with a conjugation and a Hodge structure of weights $n_1$ and $n_2$ respectively. Let $p$ and $q$ be integers. If $\varphi$ is a linear functional on $W_1$ lying in the degree-$p$ piece of the dual Hodge structure on $W_1$, and $y \in W_2$ lies in the degree-$q$ piece of the Hodge structure on $W_2$, then the rank-one linear map $W_1 \to W_2$, $x \mapsto \varphi(x)\,y$ (the image of the pure tensor $\varphi \otimes y$ under the canonical map from $W_1^* \otimes_{\mathbb{C}} W_2$ to $\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbb{C}}(W_1, W_2)$) belongs to the degree-$(p+q)$ piece of the internal Hom Hodge structure between $W_1$ and $W_2$.

name: Real.neg_log_one_sub_rpow_sub_nonneg

docstring:
For `1 < y` and `0 < s`, the quadratic remainder of `-log (1 - y ^ (-s))` is
nonnegative.
description:
**Nonnegativity of the remainder in $-\log(1-y^{-s})$.** Let $y$ and $s$ be real numbers with $y > 1$ and $s > 0$. Then
$$-\log\bigl(1 - y^{-s}\bigr) - y^{-s} \ge 0.$$
In other words, writing $x = y^{-s}$, which lies in $(0,1)$, we have $-\log(1-x) \ge x$, i.e. the first-order Taylor term $x$ is a lower bound for $-\log(1-x)$.

docstring:
An integer belongs to a height-one prime exactly when the rational prime below it divides that
integer.
description: **Membership of an integer in a height-one prime ideal.** Let $K$ be a field and let $\mathfrak p$ be a height-one prime ideal of the ring of integers of $K$. The image of an integer $n$ in the ring of integers lies in $\mathfrak p$ if and only if the rational prime lying below $\mathfrak p$ divides $n$.

name: Set.weightEnumerator_eq_sum_monomial

theorem Set.weightEnumerator_eq_sum_monomial : ∀ {ι : Type u_1} {β : ι → Type u_2} [inst : Fintype ι] [inst_1 : (i : ι) → Zero (β i)]
  [inst_2 : (i : ι) → DecidableEq (β i)] (C : Set ((i : ι) → β i)),
  C.weightEnumerator =
    ∑ w ∈ Finset.range (Fintype.card ι + 1),
      (MvPolynomial.monomial ((fun₀ | 0 => Fintype.card ι - w) + fun₀ | 1 => w)) ↑(C.weightDistribution w)
docstring: The monomial form of the weight enumerator.
description: **Weight enumerator as a sum of monomials.** Let $C$ be a set of words of length $n = |\iota|$, where each coordinate takes values in its own type with a distinguished zero. The weight enumerator of $C$ (a two-variable polynomial in $X$ and $Y$) equals $\sum_{w=0}^{n} A_w \, X^{\,n-w} Y^{\,w}$, where $A_w$ is the number of codewords in $C$ of Hamming weight $w$ (that is, with exactly $w$ nonzero coordinates). The sum runs over $w$ from $0$ to $n$, and each term is the monomial with exponent $n-w$ on $X$ and exponent $w$ on $Y$, multiplied by the coefficient $A_w$.

theorem TauCeti.NumberFieldArithmetic.artinElementAway_eq_of_isArithFrobAt : ∀ {K : Type u_1} [inst : Field K] [inst_1 : NumberField K] {L : Type u_2} [inst_2 : Field L] [inst_3 : NumberField L]
  [inst_4 : Algebra K L] [inst_5 : IsGalois K L] (hab : ∀ (σ τ : Gal(L/K)), Commute σ τ)
  (S : Finset (IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K)))
  (hur :
    ∀ v ∉ S,
      ∀ (Q : Ideal (NumberField.RingOfIntegers L)) [inst_6 : Q.IsPrime] [Q.LiesOver v.asIdeal],
        Algebra.IsUnramifiedAt (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K) Q)
  {v : IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K)},
  v ∉ S →
    ∀ (Q : Ideal (NumberField.RingOfIntegers L)) [Q.IsPrime] [Q.LiesOver v.asIdeal] {σ : Gal(L/K)},

**The Artin automorphism at `v ∉ S` is the Frobenius there.** Any arithmetic Frobenius at any
prime above `v` equals it, which is what makes the assignment `v ↦ artinElementAway hab S hur v`
well defined without a choice of prime above `v`.
description: **Equality of the Artin Map and the Arithmetic Frobenius.** Let $L/K$ be a Galois extension of number fields with an abelian Galois group $\text{Gal}(L/K)$. Let $S$ be a finite set of prime ideals of the ring of integers $\mathcal{O}_K$ containing all primes that ramify in $L$. For any prime $v$ of $\mathcal{O}_K$ not in $S$, the Artin element at $v$ is equal to any automorphism $\sigma \in \text{Gal}(L/K)$ that acts as an arithmetic Frobenius at a prime ideal $Q$ of $\mathcal{O}_L$ lying over $v$.

name: TauCeti.GLSymplecticFin.RootSubgroupIndex
signature: inductive TauCeti.GLSymplecticFin.RootSubgroupIndex : ℕ → Type
docstring:
An extensional index for the root one-parameter subgroups of the standard symplectic group.

Difference roots retain their ordered pair of indices. The symmetric positive- and negative-sum
roots store their indices in increasing order, so each root has only one index.
description: **Indices for root subgroups of the symplectic group.** For each natural number $n$, this defines a type of indices labelling the root one-parameter subgroups of the standard symplectic group of rank $n$. Difference roots are indexed by ordered pairs of indices, so the order matters. The positive-sum and negative-sum roots are indexed by unordered pairs, represented by storing the two indices in increasing order, so each such root corresponds to exactly one index.

name: TauCeti.CommHopfAlgCat.fppfQuotientHomEquiv
signature:
def TauCeti.CommHopfAlgCat.fppfQuotientHomEquiv : {R : Type u} →
  [inst : CommRing R] →
    (H : CommHopfAlgCat R) →
      (I : TauCeti.HopfIdeal R ↑H) →
        (hI : I.IsNormal) →
          (F : CategoryTheory.Grp (CategoryTheory.Sheaf (TauCeti.CommAlgCat.fppfTopology R) (Type (u + 1)))) →

docstring:
Maps from the fppf quotient sheaf to a group object in fppf sheaves are naturally equivalent
to group-object maps from the pointwise quotient presheaf to its underlying presheaf.
description: **Universal property of the fppf quotient of a commutative Hopf algebra.** Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $H$ a commutative Hopf algebra over $R$, $I$ a Hopf ideal of $H$, and assume $I$ is normal. Let $F$ be a group object in the category of fppf sheaves of sets (on commutative $R$-algebras). Then there is a natural bijection between group homomorphisms from the fppf sheafification of the quotient group $H/I$ (viewed as a group object in fppf sheaves) to $F$, and group-object homomorphisms from the pointwise quotient presheaf $H/I$ (the presheaf of groups given by the quotient at each point) to the underlying presheaf of $F$.

name: diamondOp_one
signature: theorem diamondOp_one : ∀ {N : ℕ} (k : ℤ), diamondOp k 1 = LinearMap.id
docstring: The diamond operator at `1` is the identity.
description: **Identity of the diamond operator at one.** For any integer $k$ and natural number $N$, the diamond operator $\langle 1 \rangle$ (or $\diamond 1$) acting on the space of modular forms is the identity linear map.

name: TauCeti.ModularForm.finiteDimensional_modularForm_finiteIndex

instance TauCeti.ModularForm.finiteDimensional_modularForm_finiteIndex : ∀ {𝒢 : Subgroup (GL (Fin 2) ℝ)} [inst : 𝒢.HasDetOne] [𝒢.IsFiniteRelIndex (Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup.mapGL ℝ).range]

docstring:
**Finite-dimensionality of modular forms.** As a corollary of the Sturm bound, the space
`ModularForm 𝒢 k` is finite-dimensional over `ℂ` for any subgroup `𝒢 ≤ GL(2, ℝ)` of finite
relative index in `𝒮ℒ` with determinant-one elements and discrete strict periods.
description: **Finite-dimensionality of modular forms.** Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ that has finite index relative to the image of the special linear group $\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$, whose elements all have determinant one, and whose group of strict periods is discrete. Then for every integer weight $k$, the space of modular forms of weight $k$ for $\mathcal{G}$ is a finite-dimensional vector space over $\mathbb{C}$.

name: TauCeti.UniversalEnvelopingAlgebra.kostantNumberedSymmetryCoordinateIso_hom_comp_weightTorusCoordinateMap
signature:
theorem TauCeti.UniversalEnvelopingAlgebra.kostantNumberedSymmetryCoordinateIso_hom_comp_weightTorusCoordinateMap : ∀ {V : Type} [inst : AddCommGroup V] [inst_1 : Module ℚ V] (M : AddSubgroup V) {n : ℕ} (b : Module.Basis (Fin n) ℤ ↥M)
  (θ : V ≃ₗ[ℚ] V) (hθM : ∀ (v : V), θ v ∈ M ↔ v ∈ M) {ι : Type} [inst_2 : Finite ι] (wt : Fin n → ι → ℤ)
  (basisPerm : Equiv.Perm (Fin n)) (basisScale : Fin n → ℤ),
  (∀ (i : Fin n), θ ↑(b i) = ↑(basisScale i • b (basisPerm i))) →
    CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp
        (TauCeti.UniversalEnvelopingAlgebra.kostantNumberedSymmetryCoordinateIso M b θ hθM).hom
        (TauCeti.GeneralLinear.weightTorusCoordinateMap wt) =
      TauCeti.GeneralLinear.weightTorusCoordinateMap fun i => wt (basisPerm⁻¹ i)
docstring:
**A monomial-basis numbered symmetry carries the represented weight torus of a weight family
to the weight torus of the relabelled family.** The scalar coefficients do not affect diagonal
conjugation. Stability of a closed subgroup scheme cut out by the root subgroups and a weight torus
additionally requires identifying this relabelled family with the original one, via weight
equivariance and
`GeneralLinear.weightTorusCoordinateMap_reindex`.
description: **Symmetry of Weight Torus Coordinate Maps under Monomial Basis Transformations.** Let $M$ be a lattice in a $\mathbb{Q}$-vector space $V$ with a basis $b$ indexed by $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$. Suppose a linear automorphism $\theta$ of $V$ stabilizes $M$ and acts as a monomial transformation on the basis elements, such that $\theta(b_i) = s_i \cdot b_{\sigma(i)}$ for some permutation $\sigma$ and scales $s_i \in \mathbb{Z}$. Then the composition of the induced isomorphism on the coordinate ring of the universal enveloping algebra with the weight torus coordinate map associated to a weight family $wt$ is equal to the weight torus coordinate map associated to the relabeled weight family $wt \circ \sigma^{-1}$.

name: Rep.simple_iff_isIrreducible
signature:
theorem Rep.simple_iff_isIrreducible : ∀ {k : Type u} {G : Type v} [inst : Field k] [inst_1 : Monoid G] (A : Rep.{w, u, v} k G),
  CategoryTheory.Simple A ↔ A.ρ.IsIrreducible
docstring:
**An object of `Rep k G` is simple exactly when the representation it carries is
irreducible.** Both sides say that the `k[G]`-module the object carries is simple: the left-hand
side across `Rep.equivalenceModuleMonoidAlgebra`, the right-hand side across
`Representation.irreducible_iff_isSimpleModule_asModule`.
description: **Equivalence of Simple and Irreducible Representations.** For a representation $A$ of a monoid $G$ over a field $k$, $A$ is a simple object in the category of representations $\text{Rep}(k, G)$ if and only if the representation $A.\rho$ is irreducible.

name: TauCeti.continuousSMulQuotientFixedPointsOfContinuousSMul
signature:
instance TauCeti.continuousSMulQuotientFixedPointsOfContinuousSMul : ∀ (G : Type u_1) [inst : Group G] [inst_1 : TopologicalSpace G] (M : Type u_2) [inst_2 : AddGroup M]
  [inst_3 : DistribMulAction G M] [inst_4 : TopologicalSpace M] [DiscreteTopology M] [ContinuousSMul G M]
  (H : Subgroup G) [inst_7 : H.Normal], ContinuousSMul (G ⧸ H) ↥(FixedPoints.addSubgroup (↥H) M)
docstring:
For an arbitrary normal subgroup `H`, the action of `G ⧸ H` on the invariants `M ^ H` of a
discrete module is continuous. Unlike
`TauCeti.continuousSMulQuotientFixedPoints`, which reads the continuity off the discreteness of
`G ⧸ H` for open `H` and needs no continuity of the `G`-action, this deduces it from continuity of
the `G`-action: the invariants are discrete, so continuity is continuity in the group variable
alone, and there it is the continuity of the `G`-action read through the quotient map. No
compatibility of the topology of `G` with its group structure is needed, since `G ⧸ H` carries the
quotient topology.
description: **Continuity of the induced action on invariants under a normal subgroup.** Let $G$ be a topological group (a group carrying a topology, with no compatibility assumed between the topology and the group operations), let $M$ be an additive group with a discrete topology, and suppose $G$ acts on $M$ by distributive actions such that the action map $G \times M \to M$ is continuous. Let $H$ be a normal subgroup of $G$. Then the quotient group $G/H$ acts on the subgroup $M^H$ of $H$-invariant elements of $M$, and this action is continuous when $G/H$ is given the quotient topology and $M^H$ carries the subspace topology inherited from $M$ (which is discrete). In other words, for every $G/H$-action on $M^H$ coming from the $G$-action, the scalar multiplication $(G/H) \times M^H \to M^H$ is continuous.

name: TauCeti.GraphTwistedIndex
signature: def TauCeti.GraphTwistedIndex : Type
docstring:
A valid index whose Steinberg map uses ordinary Frobenius, possibly composed with a diagram
automorphism. The Suzuki--Ree and Tits branches are excluded.
description: **Graph-twisted index.** A graph-twisted index is an index in the classification of finite groups of Lie type (a label of a twisted or untwisted Steinberg-type construction) whose associated Steinberg endomorphism is an ordinary Frobenius map, possibly composed with a graph (diagram) automorphism of the underlying root system. Such indices are exactly those in the classification that are not of Suzuki–Ree type or Tits type, which are excluded from this notion. The statement introduces this collection as a type, i.e., the set of all such admissible indices.

The augmentation of the periodic resolution is the quotient map `k[ε] ↠ k[ε]/(ε)`, read
through `TauCeti.dualNumberProjectiveResolutionXIso`.

name: TauCeti.CommHopfAlgCat.centerPointwiseQuotientMk_eq_one_iff_isCentralPoint

theorem TauCeti.CommHopfAlgCat.centerPointwiseQuotientMk_eq_one_iff_isCentralPoint : ∀ {k : Type u} [inst : Field k] (H : CommHopfAlgCat k) (A : CommAlgCat k) (g : ↑(TauCeti.HopfAlgebra.points A)),

docstring: A point maps to the identity in `G(A) / Z(G)(A)` exactly when it is universally central.
description: **Center of the points quotient.** Let $H$ be a commutative Hopf algebra over a field $k$, let $A$ be a commutative $k$-algebra, and let $G(A)$ denote the group of $A$-valued points of $H$. For any point $g \in G(A)$, its image under the canonical quotient map $G(A) \to G(A)/Z(G)(A)$, where $Z(G)(A)$ is the pointwise center, is the identity element if and only if $g$ is a universally central point, i.e., $g$ commutes with every point of $G(A')$ for every commutative $k$-algebra $A'$ (naturally in $A'$ with respect to the relevant algebra morphisms).

The CM radicand family is square-class independent: for distinct primes `p`, no nonempty
subset product of `-1, p₁, …, pₙ` is a square in `ℚ`.

orbit. This uses the orientation of `MulAction.orbitRel_apply`: the left point is a member of

description: **Product of $I$-adically Hausdorff modules.** Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $I$ an ideal of $R$, and let $\{M_i\}_{i\in\iota}$ be a family of $R$-modules, each $I$-adically Hausdorff (i.e., $\bigcap_{n\ge 1} I^n M_i = 0$ for every $i$). name: TauCeti.hermiteDilated

docstring:
The dilated Hermite polynomial `Hₙ(√2 · X)`, the polynomial whose Gaussian envelope is the
Hermite function `ψₙ`.

It is defined at this layer rather than at the basis layer because every `MemLp` result below is
already about it: `ψₙ` *is* this polynomial times `exp(-x²/2)`, up to normalization.
description: **Dilated Hermite Polynomial.** For each nonnegative integer $n$, this is the real polynomial obtained by substituting $\sqrt{2}X$ into the $n$th Hermite polynomial, namely $H_n(\sqrt{2}X)\in\mathbb{R}[X]$. It is the polynomial factor of the Hermite function $\psi_n$, which, up to normalization, equals this polynomial multiplied by $e^{-x^2/2}$.

description: **Subdiagonal Successor Property.** For any non-zero natural number $n$ and any column index $c$ in the finite set $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, applying the subdiagonal permutation of the grid to $c$ and incrementing the result by one yields the original index $c$.

name: TauCeti.PrimeBoundaryRemainder
signature:
structure TauCeti.PrimeBoundaryRemainder : (K : Type u_2) →
  [inst : Field K] →
    [NumberField K] → Set (IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum (NumberField.RingOfIntegers K)) → ℝ → Type
docstring:
**Boundary data for the prime Dirichlet series of `S`.**  The function `series` is the sum
of the Dirichlet series of `primeVonMangoldtCoeff K S` on `Re s > 1`.  The function `remainder`
is continuous on `Re s ≥ 1` and agrees on the open half-plane with
`series s - δ / (s - 1)`.

The functions have precisely their mathematically relevant domains, so the structure carries no
arbitrary values elsewhere.
description: **Boundary Data for the Prime Dirichlet Series.** For a number field $K$, a set of prime ideals $S$ in its ring of integers, and a real density $\delta$, this structure represents the analytic boundary data for the Dirichlet series associated with the prime-weighted von Mangoldt coefficients of $S$. It consists of a function `series`, defined as the sum of the Dirichlet series on the half-plane $\operatorname{Re}(s) > 1$, and a function `remainder`, which is continuous on the closed half-plane $\operatorname{Re}(s) \ge 1$. These functions are required to satisfy the relation $\text{remainder}(s) = \text{series}(s) - \frac{\delta}{s - 1}$ on the open half-plane $\operatorname{Re}(s) > 1$.

As the height tends to infinity the truncated Perron kernel tends to the sharp step, at every
positive `x`; at the endpoint `x = 1` this is the half-weight limit

name: TauCeti.IsHyperellipticFunctionField
signature: structure TauCeti.IsHyperellipticFunctionField : (k : Type u_3) → (F : Type u_4) → [inst : Field k] → [inst_1 : Field F] → [Algebra k F] → Prop
docstring:
A **hyperelliptic function field** (Stichtenoth, Definition 6.2.1, with separability of the
index-two subextension made part of the definition): genus at least two together with an element
`x` transcendental over `k` such that `F / k(x)` is separable of degree two.

Being an algebraic function field is *not* part of the predicate: the hypothesis
`TauCeti.IsFunctionField`, like the exactness of the constant field, is kept as a separate
hypothesis on the statements that need it, as everywhere in this development.

In characteristic two an index-two subextension can be purely inseparable, and such an `F` is
deliberately outside this model class; away from characteristic two the separability clause is
automatic, so there the predicate agrees with Stichtenoth's index-two definition.
description:
**Hyperelliptic function field.** Let $k$ be a field and $F$ an extension field of $k$. We say $F$ is a hyperelliptic function field over $k$ when the following two conditions hold:

1. The genus of $F$ is at least two.
2. There exists an element $x \in F$, transcendental over $k$, such that $F$ is a separable extension of the rational function field $k(x)$ of degree two.

Here the separability requirement is part of the definition, so that in characteristic two a purely inseparable quadratic subextension $F/k(x)$ does not qualify. Away from characteristic two, the separability condition holds automatically, and the notion coincides with the usual definition of a hyperelliptic function field (an index-two subextension of $F/k(x)$ of genus at least two). Note that this predicate does not itself require $F$ to be an algebraic function field over $k$, nor that $k$ be the exact constant field; such hypotheses are imposed separately wherever they are needed.

name: TauCeti.continuousSMulQuotientFixedPointsOfContinuousSMul
signature:
instance TauCeti.continuousSMulQuotientFixedPointsOfContinuousSMul : ∀ (G : Type u_1) [inst : Group G] [inst_1 : TopologicalSpace G] (M : Type u_2) [inst_2 : AddGroup M]
  [inst_3 : DistribMulAction G M] [inst_4 : TopologicalSpace M] [DiscreteTopology M] [ContinuousSMul G M]
  (H : Subgroup G) [inst_7 : H.Normal], ContinuousSMul (G ⧸ H) ↥(FixedPoints.addSubgroup (↥H) M)
docstring:
For an arbitrary normal subgroup `H`, the action of `G ⧸ H` on the invariants `M ^ H` of a
discrete module is continuous. Unlike
`TauCeti.continuousSMulQuotientFixedPoints`, which reads the continuity off the discreteness of
`G ⧸ H` for open `H` and needs no continuity of the `G`-action, this deduces it from continuity of
the `G`-action: the invariants are discrete, so continuity is continuity in the group variable
alone, and there it is the continuity of the `G`-action read through the quotient map. No
compatibility of the topology of `G` with its group structure is needed, since `G ⧸ H` carries the
quotient topology.
description: **Continuity of the Quotient Action on Invariants.** Let $G$ be a topological group and $M$ be a discrete topological additive group equipped with a continuous distributive action of $G$. For any normal subgroup $H$ of $G$, the induced action of the quotient group $G/H$ (endowed with the quotient topology) on the subgroup of $H$-invariant elements $M^H$ is continuous.

`𝔾ₐ`-point with negation in the value ring.
description: **Convolution inverse corresponds to negation.** Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $A$ a commutative $R$-algebra. A $\mathbb{G}_a$-point is an $R$-algebra homomorphism from the symmetric algebra of $R$ over $R$ to $A$, and these form a group under the convolution product. For any such point $F$, the image of its convolution inverse $F^{-1}$ under the identification $\mathrm{gaPointsMulEquiv}$ equals the inverse (in the target group, which is the additive group of the value ring $A$) of the image of $F$. In other words, the identification sends convolution inverses to additive negatives in $A$.

  (S : TauCeti.Semigroups.StronglyContinuousSemigroup X) (lambda t : ℝ),

docstring: Real-time form of the shifted operator at nonnegative times.
description:
**Shifted Semigroup Real-Time Operator Formula.** Let $X$ be a real normed vector space and let $S$ be a strongly continuous semigroup on $X$. For any real parameter $\lambda$ and any nonnegative time $t \ge 0$, the real-time operator of the semigroup obtained by shifting $S$ by $\lambda$ is given by multiplying the original real-time operator of $S$ at time $t$ by the scalar $e^{-\lambda t}$. Equivalently, if $S_\lambda(t)$ denotes the real-time operator of the shifted semigroup and $S(t)$ denotes the real-time operator of $S$, then
\[
S_\lambda(t) = e^{-\lambda t} S(t).
\]

exactly two: the inertia subgroup at a ramified prime is as small as it can be.

the prime (`isUnramifiedIn_adjoin_range_ne_primeDiscriminantPrime`), so the absolute ramification

theorem TauCeti.UniversalEnvelopingAlgebra.kostantNumberedSymmetryCoordinateIso_hom_comp_weightTorusCoordinateMap : ∀ {V : Type} [inst : AddCommGroup V] [inst_1 : Module ℚ V] (M : AddSubgroup V) {n : ℕ} (b : Module.Basis (Fin n) ℤ ↥M)

  (∀ (i : Fin n), θ ↑(b i) = ↑(basisScale i • b (basisPerm i))) →
    CategoryTheory.CategoryStruct.comp
        (TauCeti.UniversalEnvelopingAlgebra.kostantNumberedSymmetryCoordinateIso M b θ hθM).hom

docstring:
**A monomial-basis numbered symmetry carries the represented weight torus of a weight family
to the weight torus of the relabelled family.** The scalar coefficients do not affect diagonal
conjugation. Stability of a closed subgroup scheme cut out by the root subgroups and a weight torus
additionally requires identifying this relabelled family with the original one, via weight
equivariance and
`GeneralLinear.weightTorusCoordinateMap_reindex`.
description: **Numbered symmetry intertwines weight torus coordinates.** Let $V$ be a $\mathbb{Q}$-vector space, $M \subseteq V$ an additive subgroup with a $\mathbb{Z}$-basis $(b_i)_{i \in \{1,\dots,n\}}$, and $\theta$ a $\mathbb{Q}$-linear automorphism of $V$ that preserves $M$ (so $\theta(v) \in M$ exactly when $v \in M$). Let $\iota$ be a finite index type, and let $\mathrm{wt}_i : \iota \to \mathbb{Z}$ be a family of integer weight vectors indexed by $i$. Suppose $\sigma$ is a permutation of the indices and $c_i \in \mathbb{Z}$ are integer scalars such that $\theta(b_i) = c_i \, b_{\sigma(i)}$ for every $i$. Then, composing the coordinate isomorphism induced by $\theta$ on $M$ (the Kostant-numbered symmetry isomorphism) with the weight torus coordinate map for the family $\mathrm{wt}$ gives the same result as applying the weight torus coordinate map to the reindexed family $i \mapsto \mathrm{wt}_{\sigma^{-1}(i)}$. name: ContinuousLinearMap.exists_localStableSetHomeomorph
signature:
theorem ContinuousLinearMap.exists_localStableSetHomeomorph : ∀ {X : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup X] [inst_1 : NormedSpace ℝ X] [CompleteSpace X] {K α ε : NNReal}
  (A P : X →L[ℝ] X) (N : X → X) (r : ℝ),
  (∀ (t : ℝ), 0 ≤ t → ∀ (v : X), ‖(NormedSpace.exp (t • A)) (P v)‖ ≤ ↑K * Real.exp (-↑α * t) * ‖v‖) →
    (∀ t ≤ 0, ∀ (v : X), ‖(NormedSpace.exp (t • A)) (v - P v)‖ ≤ ↑K * Real.exp (↑α * t) * ‖v‖) →
      LipschitzOnWith ε N (Metric.closedBall 0 r) →
        2 * K * (ε * 2) < α →
          N 0 = 0 →
            IsIdempotentElem P →
              Commute A P →
                0 < r →
                  ∃ ρ > 0,
                    Nonempty
                      (↑{v | ‖↑v‖ ≤ ρ} ≃ₜ
                        ↑{z |
                            (∃ y,
                                IsIntegralCurveOn y (fun x w => A w + N w) (Set.Ici 0) ∧
                                  y 0 = z ∧ Set.MapsTo y (Set.Ici 0) (Metric.closedBall 0 r)) ∧
                              ‖P z‖ ≤ ρ})
docstring:
For a small enough truncation radius, the local stable set of confined forward solutions is
homeomorphic to a closed ball in the stable spectral subspace.
description: **Homeomorphism between the Stable Subspace and the Local Stable Set.** Let $A$ be a continuous linear operator on a Banach space $X$, and let $P$ be a continuous projection that commutes with $A$. Suppose that $P$ defines a hyperbolic splitting such that the flow $e^{tA}$ is contracted by $K e^{-\alpha t}$ on the range of $P$ for $t \ge 0$, and is contracted by $K e^{\alpha t}$ on the kernel of $P$ for $t \le 0$. Let $N$ be a nonlinearity such that $N(0) = 0$ and $N$ is Lipschitz continuous on a closed ball of radius $r > 0$ with a sufficiently small Lipschitz constant $\varepsilon$ satisfying $4K\varepsilon < \alpha$. Then there exists a radius $\rho > 0$ such that the set of initial conditions $z$ whose forward integral curves under the vector field $Aw + N(w)$ remain within the ball of radius $r$ for all $t \ge 0$, and which satisfy $\|Pz\| \le \rho$, is homeomorphic to the closed ball of radius $\rho$ in the stable subspace $\text{ran}(P)$.

name: TauCeti.spechtModule_ones_ρ_apply

  ((TauCeti.spechtModule (TauCeti.Nat.Partition.ones n)).ρ σ) x = ↑↑(Equiv.Perm.sign σ) • x
docstring:
**`S^{(1ⁿ)}` is the sign representation**: the symmetric group acts on it through the sign
character.  The sign is unchanged by the relabelling `Fin n ≃ Fin (diagramOf (1ⁿ)).card` that
`TauCeti.spechtModule` transports along.

This is not a `simp` lemma, for the reason given at
`TauCeti.spechtModule_indiscrete_ρ_apply`.
description: **The Specht module of the partition $(1^n)$ is the sign representation.** For any natural number $n$, the action of the symmetric group $S_n$ on the Specht module $S^{(1^n)}$ is given by the sign character. Specifically, for any permutation $\sigma \in S_n$ and any element $x$ in the module, the representation $\rho(\sigma)$ maps $x$ to $\text{sgn}(\sigma) \cdot x$.

name: TauCeti.lie_eq_smul_heisenbergZ
signature:
theorem TauCeti.lie_eq_smul_heisenbergZ : ∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : CommRing R] (A B : ↥(TauCeti.heisenberg R)),
  ⁅A, B⁆ = (↑A 0 1 * ↑B 1 2 - ↑B 0 1 * ↑A 1 2) • TauCeti.heisenbergZ R
docstring:
**The bracket of the Heisenberg Lie algebra is a multiple of its central generator.** The
coefficient is the `2 × 2` determinant of the two superdiagonal entries, so the whole bracket
structure of the strict upper triangle in size three is one `2 × 2` determinant.
description:
**Bracket in the Heisenberg Lie algebra.** Let $R$ be a commutative ring, and let $\mathfrak{h}$ be the Heisenberg Lie algebra over $R$, realized as the strictly upper triangular $3\times 3$ matrices with the commutator bracket. For any two elements $A, B \in \mathfrak{h}$, the bracket $[A,B]$ is a scalar multiple of the central generator $Z$. Specifically,
$$[A,B] = \left(A_{01}B_{12} - B_{01}A_{12}\right) Z,$$
where $A_{01}, A_{12}$ and $B_{01}, B_{12}$ are the superdiagonal entries of $A$ and $B$. The coefficient is therefore the $2\times 2$ determinant formed from the two superdiagonal entries of $A$ and $B$.

docstring: The conjugacy class associated to a partition of `n` has that partition.
description: **Conjugacy classes recover their partitions.** For every natural number $n$ and every partition $p$ of $n$, take the conjugacy class of permutations in the symmetric group on $n$ points that corresponds to $p$ under the standard bijection between partitions of $n$ and conjugacy classes. Then the partition associated with that conjugacy class (by cycle type) is exactly $p$. In other words, the map sending a conjugacy class to its cycle-type partition is a left inverse of the bijection from partitions to conjugacy classes.

description: **Projection onto the first factor of an orthogonal sum.** Let $V$ and $W$ be rational vector spaces, and let $L$ and $M$ be integral lattices in $V$ and $W$ respectively. The dilated Hermite polynomial `Hₙ(√2 · X)`, the polynomial whose Gaussian envelope is the

`TauCeti.simpleRepSelfEquiv` and `TauCeti.kroneckerProjSrcEquiv`.

Take any element $y$ of the underlying vector space at the source vertex of the indecomposable projective representation $P_1$. name: TauCeti.isOpen_image_schwarzChristoffelPrimitive

theorem TauCeti.isOpen_image_schwarzChristoffelPrimitive : ∀ {ι : Type u_1} [inst : Fintype ι] (a e : ι → ℝ) (z₀ : UpperHalfPlane) {s : Set ℂ},
  IsOpen s → s ⊆ UpperHalfPlane.upperHalfPlaneSet → IsOpen (TauCeti.schwarzChristoffelPrimitive a e z₀ '' s)
docstring:
**The Schwarz--Christoffel primitive is an open map on the upper half-plane.**  Its derivative
is the integrand, which never vanishes there, so the inverse function theorem makes the image of
every neighbourhood a neighbourhood.
description: **Schwarz–Christoffel primitive is open on the upper half-plane.** Let $\iota$ be a finite index set, and let $a = (a_i)_{i\in\iota}$ and $e = (e_i)_{i\in\iota}$ be families of real numbers. Fix a base point $z_0$ in the upper half-plane. Then for every open subset $s$ of the complex plane that is contained in the upper half-plane, the image of $s$ under the Schwarz–Christoffel primitive (the map defined from these data and the base point $z_0$) is again open in $\mathbb{C}$. In other words, the Schwarz–Christoffel primitive is an open map when restricted to the upper half-plane. This follows because its derivative, the Schwarz–Christoffel integrand, never vanishes there, so the map is locally invertible by the inverse function theorem.

            ∀ (i : ι) (𝔓 : Ideal (NumberField.RingOfIntegers L)) [𝔓.IsPrime]
              [𝔓.LiesOver (Ideal.span {↑(TauCeti.Multiquadratic.primeDiscriminantPrime (D i))})],
              𝔓.ramificationIdx ℤ = 2
docstring:
**The ramification index at a ramified prime of a prime-discriminant compositum is `2`.**
However many factors the compositum has, a prime belonging to one of them has ramification index
exactly two: the inertia subgroup at a ramified prime is as small as it can be.

The upper bound is transverse cancellation. The compositum `U` of the other roots is unramified at
the prime (`isUnramifiedIn_adjoin_range_ne_primeDiscriminantPrime`), so the absolute ramification
index equals the relative one over `U`, which is at most `[L : U] = 2`. The lower bound is the
total ramification of the quadratic subfield `ℚ(root i)`.
description: **Ramification Index of a Prime-Discriminant Compositum.** Let $L$ be a number field formed by the compositum of quadratic extensions $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{d_i})$ for a finite set of distinct prime discriminants $d_i$. Specifically, assume $L = \mathbb{Q}(\{\sqrt{d_i^*}\}_{i \in \iota})$ where each $d_i$ is a prime discriminant, the map $i \mapsto d_i$ is injective, at most one $d_i$ is even, and $d_i^*$ denotes the radicand associated with the discriminant $d_i$. For any index $i$, let $p_i$ be the unique prime number dividing the discriminant $d_i$. If $\mathfrak{P}$ is a prime ideal of the ring of integers of $L$ lying over the principal ideal $(p_i)$ in $\mathbb{Z}$, then the absolute ramification index of $\mathfrak{P}$ over $\mathbb{Z}$ is exactly $2$.

**Upper tail of the second Euler beta integral.** Let $a, b, u_0$ be real numbers with $0 \le u_0 < 1$. Then

theorem TauCeti.Probability.blockLaw_def : ∀ {Ω : Type u_1} {α : Type u_2} {ι : Type u_4} [inst : MeasurableSpace Ω] [inst_1 : MeasurableSpace α]
  (μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω) (X : ι → Ω → α) {m : ℕ} (k : Fin m → ι),
  TauCeti.Probability.blockLaw μ X k = MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun ω i => X (k i) ω) μ
description: **Block law definition.** Let $(\Omega, \mathcal{F})$ and $(\alpha, \mathcal{A})$ be measurable spaces, let $\mu$ be a measure on $\Omega$, let $(X_i)_{i \in \iota}$ be a family of $\alpha$-valued functions on $\Omega$, and let $k = (k_1, \dots, k_m)$ be a finite list of indices from $\iota$. The block law of $(X_i)$ along $k$ with respect to $\mu$ is the image (pushforward) measure of $\mu$ under the map $\omega \mapsto (X_{k_1}(\omega), \dots, X_{k_m}(\omega))$ sending $\Omega$ to $\alpha^m$. In other words, the block law is the distribution of the finite subfamily $(X_{k_i})_{i=1}^m$ under $\mu$.
