name: WeierstrassCurve.Coeff
signature: inductive WeierstrassCurve.Coeff : Type
docstring:
A type whose elements represent the five coefficients `a₁`, `a₂`, `a₃`, `a₄` and `a₆` of the
Weierstrass polynomial. It indexes the variables of `MvPolynomial Coeff ℤ = ℤ[A₁,⋯,A₆]`, the ring
the universal curve is defined over. There is no `A₅` — the subscripts are weights, not positions —
and the constructors are uppercase as names of indeterminates: `specialize` sends `A₁` to `W.a₁`.
description: **Weierstrass curve coefficient index.** A type indexing the five coefficients $a_1,a_2,a_3,a_4,a_6$ of the Weierstrass polynomial. Its elements serve as the indeterminates $A_1,A_2,A_3,A_4,A_6$ in the universal coefficient ring $\mathbb{Z}[A_1,\ldots,A_6]$, over which the universal curve is defined. The index $5$ is omitted because the subscripts denote weights rather than positions; under specialization, the indeterminate corresponding to index $1$ is sent to the $a_1$-coefficient of a given curve.

name: Matrix.pairMinor_transpose
signature:
theorem Matrix.pairMinor_transpose : ∀ {m : Type u_1} {n : Type u_2} {R : Type u} [inst : CommRing R] (g : Matrix m n R) (p : m × m) (q : n × n),
  g.transpose.pairMinor q p = g.pairMinor p q
docstring:
A minor of the transpose is the minor of the matrix with the row and column pairs
exchanged.
description: **Transpose of a pair minor.** Let $g$ be an $m \times n$ matrix over a commutative ring $R$, let $p = (p_1, p_2)$ be a pair of row indices from $m$, and let $q = (q_1, q_2)$ be a pair of column indices from $n$. Taking the pair minor of the transpose $g^{T}$ with row pair $q$ and column pair $p$ gives the same result as taking the pair minor of $g$ with row pair $p$ and column pair $q$. In other words, transposing a matrix simply exchanges the roles of the row and column pairs in forming a pair minor.

name: LinearEquiv.map_range_of_intertwine
signature:
theorem LinearEquiv.map_range_of_intertwine : ∀ {R : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} {N : Type u_3} [inst : Semiring R] [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid M] [inst_2 : AddCommMonoid N]
  [inst_3 : Module R M] [inst_4 : Module R N] (e : M ≃ₗ[R] N) (f : M →ₗ[R] M) (g : N →ₗ[R] N),
  (∀ (d : M), g (e d) = e (f d)) → Submodule.map (↑e) f.range = g.range
docstring:
If a linear equivalence `e` intertwines two endomorphisms `f` and `g` pointwise
(`g (e d) = e (f d)`), it carries the range of `f` onto the range of `g`.
description: **Range preservation under an intertwining linear equivalence.** Let $R$ be a semiring and let $M$ and $N$ be $R$-modules. Suppose $e:M\to N$ is a linear equivalence, and let $f:M\to M$ and $g:N\to N$ be linear endomorphisms satisfying $g(e(d))=e(f(d))$ for every $d\in M$. Then $e$ maps the range of $f$ onto the range of $g$; equivalently, $e(f(M))=g(N)$.

The coordinates `1, i, j, k` are an isometry from the norm form of `ℍ[R,a,b]` to the diagonal

name: TauCeti.Hodge.HodgeStructureOn.dualTensorHom_mem_internalHom_piece
docstring:
A rank-one map made from a dual vector of degree `p` and a target vector of degree `q` has
internal-hom degree `p + q`.
description: **Degree of Rank-One Maps in Internal Hom Hodge Structures.** Given two complex vector spaces $W_1$ and $W_2$ equipped with Hodge structures of weights $n_1$ and $n_2$ respectively, let $\phi$ be a linear functional in the $p$-th piece of the dual Hodge structure on $W_1$, and let $y$ be an element in the $q$-th piece of the Hodge structure on $W_2$. An ideal arithmetic function is multiplicative when it takes the unit ideal to `1` and
respects products of relatively prime nonzero ideals. This is weaker than the complete
multiplicativity carried by `MultiplicativeIdealWeight`.

of invariant subspaces, so one is irreducible exactly when the other is.

Conjugation by `g` is an autoequivalence of `FDRep k N`, with inverse conjugation by `g⁻¹`:

docstring:
**The rational places of `k(x)` are `ℙ¹(k) = k ∪ {∞}`** (Stichtenoth, Corollary 1.2.3): a
place of `k(x)` has degree one exactly when it is the place at infinity or the place of a linear
polynomial `X - a`.

Under this correspondence, an element $a \in k$ maps to the place associated with the linear polynomial $x - a$, while the element $\infty$ maps to the place at infinity.

`X ⟪Y, Z⟫ = ⟪∇_X Y, Z⟫ + ⟪Y, ∇_X Z⟫`: this is
`CovariantDerivative.IsMetricCompatible.mvfderiv_inner_eq` read off the defining property
`IsLeviCivitaConnection.isMetricCompatible`.
description:
**Metric compatibility of the Levi-Civita connection.** Let $M$ be a smooth manifold modeled on a finite-dimensional real normed space, equipped with a Riemannian metric (inner products on tangent spaces varying smoothly), and let $
abla$ be a covariant derivative on the tangent bundle that is a Levi-Civita connection. Let $Y$ and $Z$ be (sufficiently smooth, at least $C^1$-type differentiable at $x$) vector fields on $M$, and let $X$ be any vector field. Then, at the point $x$, the derivative of the function $y \mapsto \langle Y(y), Z(y)angle$ in the direction $X(x)$ equals
$$X\langle Y, Zangle(x) = \langle 
abla_X Y(x), Z(x)angle + \langle Y(x), 
abla_X Z(x)angle.$$

The bigraded `Ext` groups of `(X, Y)` **assemble into the ungraded `Ext` groups** of a pair
`(X', Y')`: in every cohomological degree the direct sum over the internal degrees of
`Ext^n(X, Y{j})` is `Ext^n(X', Y')`.

characteristic.  A functor forgetting the grading supplies the intended pairs `(U X, U Y)`; the
existence of such a functor, or even of a shift-compatible one, does not by itself supply these
isomorphisms.

Suppose $\sigma$ is an autoequivalence of $C$ playing the role of the internal grading shift, $X, Y$ are objects of $C$, and $X', Y'$ are objects of $D$. The statement asserts that the bigraded Ext groups of $(X, Y)$ assemble into the ungraded Ext groups of $(X', Y')$: for every cohomological degree $n$, the direct sum over internal degrees $j$ of $\operatorname{Ext}^n(X, \sigma^j Y)$ is isomorphic to $\operatorname{Ext}^n(X', Y')$. This is an extra hypothesis that is not automatic from the existence of a forgetful functor.

theorem TauCeti.torusCharacter_sub : ∀ {κ : Type v} {R : Type w} [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : Fintype κ] (s : κ → Rˣ) (μ ν : κ → ℤ),
  TauCeti.torusCharacter s (μ - ν) = TauCeti.torusCharacter s μ / TauCeti.torusCharacter s ν
docstring: Subtracting weights divides the values of their characters.
description:
**Torus characters turn differences of weights into quotients.** Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $\kappa$ a finite index set, and $s = (s_i)_{i\in\kappa}$ a family of units of $R$. For integer weight vectors $\mu, 
u \in \mathbb{Z}^\kappa$, the character of $s$ at the difference $\mu - 
u$ equals the character at $\mu$ divided by the character at $
u$. Here the character at a weight $\mu$ is the product $\prod_{i\in\kappa} s_i^{\mu_i}$, so the identity reads $\prod_i s_i^{\mu_i - 
u_i} =  ig(\prod_i s_i^{\mu_i} ig) ig(\prod_i s_i^{
u_i} ig)^{-1}$.

name: TauCeti.SheafOfModules.isFiniteType_biprod

description: **Direct sum of finite type sheaves of modules.** Let $C$ be a category equipped with a Grothendieck topology $J$, and let $R$ be a sheaf of rings on $(C, J)$. Assume the standard sheafification and locally-bijective hypotheses hold (for $C$ and for each slice $C/X$), and that $C$ has pullbacks. If $M$ and $N$ are sheaves of $R$-modules that are each of finite type, then their direct sum (biproduct) $M \oplus N$ is also a sheaf of $R$-modules of finite type.

  (∀ (i : ι), Nat.Prime (p i)) →
    Function.Injective p →
      ∀ (S : Finset (Option ι)), S.Nonempty → ¬IsSquare (∏ x ∈ S, TauCeti.Multiquadratic.cmRadicand p x)
docstring:
The CM radicand family is square-class independent: for distinct primes `p`, no nonempty
subset product of `-1, p₁, …, pₙ` is a square in `ℚ`.
description: **Square-Class Independence of the CM Radicand Family.** Let $p: \iota \to \mathbb{N}$ be an injective sequence of prime numbers. For any $i \in \iota$, let the radicands be defined by the family $\{-1\} \cup \{p_i\}_{i \in \iota}$. Then, the product of any non-empty finite subset of these radicands is never a square in $\mathbb{Q}$.
